trust_decision.summary: Whether an IPv6 literal that embeds a routable IPv4 address (IPv4-mapped ::ffff:0:0/96 or NAT64 well-known 64:ff9b::/96) is treated as loopback/link-local/private/CGNAT/broadcast/unspecified, i.e. whether an SSRF allow-list built on Address6's special-property checks can be steered into internal space, is decided by Address6's property checks and by the TYPES table that getType() consults - not by the parser.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names 'IPv4-mapped/NAT64', and isMapped4() is the only method in the tree that names that concept; README:233 links straight to it. It sits ~25 lines above the special-property checks that never call it.

fix_sites.entry_point: new Address6(host).embeddedIPv4() (new method, inserted after src/ipv6.ts:1245)
new Address6(host).getType() (TYPES gains '::ffff:0:0/96' at the line-46 insertion point)
embeddedIPv4() constant NAT64_WELL_KNOWN_SUBNET = 64:ff9b::/96 (appended to the module-level subnet list)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the constants table only feeds the display label from getType(), so the property checks can all be fixed inside src/ipv6.ts and the TYPES edit skipped; the same argument extends to 'getScope() is multicast scope, not a trust check' and '6to4/Teredo need a relay, the advisory names only mapped and NAT64'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Embedded-IPv4 extraction must stay gated on mapped-or-well-known-NAT64 and must not reclassify native addresses whose trailing 32 bits happen to look internal: with to4() applied unconditionally 2001:db8::a9fe:a9fe would read link-local and fe80::a9fe:a9fe link-local; the fix also deliberately returns null for NAT64 local-use 64:ff9b:1::/48, and isULA() must stay fc00::/7-only rather than absorbing ::ffff:10.0.0.1 (documented at README:237).

O6_input_shapes: NAT64 with a dotted-quad suffix (64:ff9b::127.0.0.1), which the parser accepts via parse4in6
mapped public addresses that must stay global (::ffff:8.8.8.8)
native IPv6 unchanged (::1, ::, fe80::1, fc00::1, ff02::1, 2001:db8::1)
NAT64 local-use 64:ff9b:1::/48 deliberately excluded from extraction

O7_producer.where: src/ipv6.ts:735-773 (parse4in6 sets this.address4/this.v4 only when the literal was written with a dotted-quad tail)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Address6.getScope() returns 'Global' for ::ffff:127.0.0.1 and 64:ff9b::7f00:1 both before and after the fix; a guard that allows scope==='Global' is still bypassed
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: getScope() is RFC 4007 multicast/unicast scope, not a trust-boundary check; the advisory names the boolean property checks
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~700 lines from the checks

O8_uncovered_routes.route: 6to4 (2002:7f00:0001::) and Teredo (2001::/32) literals embed an IPv4 gateway/client address that embeddedIPv4() never extracts, so isLoopback/isLinkLocal/isPrivate stay false for them
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: 6to4/Teredo need a relay or tunnel endpoint, and the advisory names only IPv4-mapped and NAT64; the repo exposes them as separate inspect*/is* features

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A literal carrying a CIDR prefix is still misclassified: new Address6('::ffff:127.0.0.1/96').isLoopback() is false because isInSubnet() bails when this.subnetMask < 96 (common.ts:10) so isMapped4() is false, and when it does reach to4() a /96 prefix yields Address4 127.0.0.1/0 whose checks all fail
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a URL host literal never carries a CIDR prefix, so prefixed input is an unsupported shape
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: cause sits in a different module (src/common.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Addresses produced by Address6.fromAddress4Nat64(v4, '64:ff9b:1::/48') (or any RFC 6052 prefix other than /96) are not normalised: embeddedIPv4() hardcodes 64:ff9b::/96 and takes the trailing 32 bits, while the repo's own toAddress4Nat64(prefix) knows how to split the octets around the reserved bits for /32-/64
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: local-use NAT64 / non-/96 prefixes are an unsupported combination and the trailing-32 shortcut is deliberately not applied there
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, encoder/decoder pair ~200 lines from the checks

O8b_injection_room.sibling: toAddress4Nat64(prefix) / fromAddress4Nat64(prefix) sibling that normalises any RFC 6052 prefix length, not just /96
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the encoder/decoder pair already supports /32,/40,/48,/56,/64,/96 and is the obvious primitive a maintainer would reuse instead of a second hardcoded /96 shortcut

O8b_injection_room.sibling: inspect6to4()/inspectTeredo() returning an embedded Address4 that the property checks consult
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both methods already decode an embedded IPv4 and the codebase's stated reason for the fix (classify a literal by what it reaches) applies verbatim to them

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second producer that fills this.address4/this.v4 for hex-notation mapped literals so object state matches the property checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the parser currently produces address4 only for dotted-quad input, and is4() (README:232) exposes that notation-level asymmetry, so a maintainer could extend parse4in6

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-prefix classification flag in TYPES (e.g. 'internal: true') that embeddedIPv4() and getType() both read
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix already had to add one row to this table, so enriching rows rather than hardcoding subnets in ipv6.ts is a natural next maintainer step

O9_family: IP-literal misclassification / SSRF guard bypass (CWE-20 improper input validation, CWE-918 SSRF) - an embedded IPv4 is never normalised before the trust decision

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 12 (package.json engines), tsc <5.6 for build, mocha 11 + tsx + source-map-support via .mocharc.yml, c8 for coverage
O10_build.project_tests: mocha specs in test/*.ts; test/functionality-v6-test.ts already covers isMapped4 with both notations (1099-1137), the is4/isMapped4 differential (1128-1136), NAT64 getType (87-92), getScope (35-69) and isULA (1069-1082); the file ends at 1244, so none of the fix's new regression block exists at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add 'if (this.isMapped4()) return this.to4().isX()' to each existing check - covers ::ffff:0:0/96 in every notation but leaves all 64:ff9b::/96 NAT64 literals global and never adds isPrivate/isCGNAT/isBroadcast.

out_of_scope_notes: Not pursued: the href()/link() HTML builders in the same class use helpers.escapeHtml and are unrelated to this advisory; no other security-relevant observation was made outside the address-classification scope.
